name: Cliff Obrecht
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Fusion Books in 2007 with Melanie Perkins, an online yearbook design platform that became the largest yearbook company in Australia and New Zealand and validated the product thesis later scaled into Canva.
early_history_summary: Obrecht grew up in Kingsley, a Perth suburb; his father Stan was a government employee and his mother Mary a school teacher. He studied Arts and Education at the University of Western Australia, where he met Melanie Perkins in 2006. In 2007 they launched Fusion Books from Perkins's mother's living room, building a drag-and-drop yearbook editor that proved there was demand for simplified online design tools.
family_context_summary: Born to Stan Obrecht, a government employee, and Mary Obrecht, a school teacher; grew up in Kingsley near Perth. Middle-class public-sector household with no documented tech or startup platform.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as tech or design industry; mother was a school teacher and father a government employee.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Melanie Perkins partnership, Fusion Books proof-of-concept, Perth living-room startup
evidence_summary: Obrecht co-founded Fusion Books at about age 21 with university partner Melanie Perkins, running an online yearbook business that grew into the largest in Australia and New Zealand. Family background is middle-class Perth (teacher mother, government-employee father) with no clear inherited capital or tech network. The durable cofounder partnership with Perkins was the central early advantage; they later recruited Cameron Adams and launched Canva in 2012–2013. Geography was a disadvantage versus Silicon Valley, and they faced extensive investor rejection before Canva scaled.
starting_point: Born and raised in Kingsley, Perth, Western Australia, to a government-employee father and school-teacher mother; middle-class public-sector household.
current_position: Co-founder and COO of Canva; joint net worth with Melanie Perkins assessed around A$14 billion (AFR 2025) / ~US$7.6 billion each (Forbes early 2026).

trajectory.event: Co-founded Fusion Books with Melanie Perkins, an online yearbook design platform that became the largest in Australia and New Zealand.
Joined by third co-founder Cameron Adams and began building Canva as a general-purpose online design platform.
Public launch of Canva in Sydney after extensive investor rejections.
Married Melanie Perkins on Rottnest Island; the couple joined the Giving Pledge.
Appeared with Perkins as among Australia's wealthiest people on the AFR Rich List with joint net worth around A$14 billion.

name: Vlad Tenev
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Robinhood in 2012–2013 with Baiju Bhatt to offer commission-free stock trading, after earlier fintech startups Celeris (2010) and Chronos Research (2011).
early_history_summary: Born in Varna, Bulgaria, Tenev joined his World Bank–employed parents in the U.S. at age five and grew up in the Washington, D.C. area. He attended Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology, earned a BS in mathematics from Stanford (where he met Baiju Bhatt), and an MS in mathematics from UCLA before dropping out of a PhD track to build trading-tech startups. By 2012–2013, at age 25–26, he co-founded Robinhood.
family_context_summary: Bulgarian immigrant family; parents both worked at the World Bank after his father pursued U.S. graduate study. Household was frugal, shaped by financial instability in Bulgaria, but offered educational stability in suburban Virginia.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents worked at the World Bank (international finance/development), providing indirect exposure to finance and a professional immigrant path, though not direct brokerage or trading-domain apprenticeship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford math, UCLA MS, TJHSST, Baiju Bhatt cofounder, World Bank parents, prior HFT startups
evidence_summary: Tenev combined elite quantitative training (Stanford/UCLA math, selective science high school) with two earlier fintech experiments (Celeris, Chronos) before co-founding Robinhood at about age 25–26. Parents at the World Bank gave immigrant educational stability and finance-adjacent context without inherited brokerage capital. High-trust partnership with Bhatt and direct exposure to HFT/latency software shaped product insight for commission-free retail trading, riding the smartphone-brokerage wave.
starting_point: Born in Varna, Bulgaria; joined World Bank–employed parents in the U.S. at age five and grew up frugally in the Washington, D.C. area after early separation from immigrant parents.
current_position: Chairman and CEO of Robinhood Markets; co-founder and executive chairman of AI company Harmonic; Forbes-listed billionaire.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Celeris, a high-frequency trading software company in New York with Baiju Bhatt.
Launched Chronos Research, selling low-latency trading software to banks and trading firms.
Co-founded Robinhood to offer commission-free retail stock trading; waitlist grew rapidly after the brokerage announcement.
Became a billionaire after a funding round valued Robinhood at about $6 billion.
Became sole CEO of Robinhood after previously sharing the role with Bhatt.
Led Robinhood through IPO at roughly $32 billion valuation; testified before Congress after GameStop trading halt.
Co-founded Harmonic, a mathematical AI reasoning company, as executive chairman.

name: Baiju Bhatt
milestone_by_age_26: No material age-26 milestone found. Co-founded Robinhood in 2012–2013 at about age 28–29; earlier Celeris (2010) and Chronos Research (2011) were small/abandoned or niche HFT tools without independent public notability comparable to Robinhood.
early_history_summary: Son of Gujarati Indian immigrants; grew up in Poquoson, Virginia, where his father worked at NASA Langley Research Center. Earned a physics bachelor's and mathematics master's at Stanford, meeting Vlad Tenev there, then built early trading-tech startups before Robinhood.
family_context_summary: Son of Gujarati Indian immigrants in Poquoson, Virginia; father worked at NASA Langley Research Center.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father's NASA engineering work sparked Bhatt's interest in space (later relevant to Aetherflux/Cowboy Space) but is not a direct fintech apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Bhatt's defining public achievement is co-founding Robinhood at roughly age 28–29. Pre-Robinhood companies Celeris and Chronos document early fintech experimentation but lack the scale or independent recognition needed as age-26 material milestones under a conservative reading.

name: Jan Koum
milestone_by_age_26: No material age-26 milestone found. Fame arrived with WhatsApp, incorporated on his 33rd birthday in 2009; earlier Yahoo! infrastructure engineering (from ~1997, age 21) was standard employment rather than an independently notable breakout.
early_history_summary: Born in Kyiv to a Jewish family and raised in Fastiv; immigrated to Mountain View, California at 16 with his mother and grandmother, working as a grocery cleaner while his mother babysat. Self-taught programming, briefly attended San Jose State, worked security testing at Ernst & Young, then joined Yahoo! as an infrastructure engineer in 1997.
family_context_summary: Immigrated from Ukraine at 16 into poverty; mother worked as a babysitter; father remained in Ukraine and died in 1997; mother died of cancer in 2000.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father worked in construction; no tech domain transfer documented.
evidence_summary: Koum's defining achievement—co-founding WhatsApp and the later Facebook acquisition—occurred at age 33. Pre-26 career consists of immigrant hardship, self-taught programming, and Yahoo! engineering employment, which does not meet the material independent-milestone bar.

name: Brian Acton
milestone_by_age_26: No material age-26 milestone found. WhatsApp co-founding was in 2009 at about age 37; earlier Stanford CS degree (1994) and Yahoo! employment from 1996 (age ~24) were career-building jobs, not independently notable breakouts.
early_history_summary: Grew up in Michigan and Central Florida; graduated Lake Howell High School, briefly attended University of Pennsylvania on scholarship, then Stanford CS (1994). Worked systems administration at Rockwell and product testing at Apple and Adobe before joining Yahoo! in 1996, where he later worked with Jan Koum.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond Michigan/Florida upbringing.
evidence_summary: Acton's defining milestones—WhatsApp co-founding and the Facebook acquisition, then Signal Foundation—occurred well after age 26. Pre-26 activity is elite education and industry employment without a dated personal product or company breakout.

name: Gavin Wood
milestone_by_age_26: No material age-26 milestone found. Ethereum co-founding and Yellow Paper work occurred around 2013–2014 (age ~33–34); PhD completion in 2005 and prior Microsoft research scientist work are academic/employment steps, not independently material public breakouts by 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Lancaster, England; attended Lancaster Royal Grammar School; earned MEng from University of York (2002) and PhD on content-based musical audio visualization (2005). Worked as a research scientist at Microsoft before joining the Ethereum founding effort with Vitalik Buterin and others.
evidence_summary: Wood's defining work—Ethereum co-founding, EVM/Yellow Paper/Solidity, Web3 coinage, and later Polkadot—began in his early thirties. No independently verifiable material public milestone by age 26 was identified.

name: Changpeng Zhao
milestone_by_age_26: No material age-26 milestone found. Binance launched in 2017 at about age 40; earlier career includes McGill CS, Bloomberg Tradebook engineering, and founding Fusion Systems in Shanghai around 2005 (age ~28).
early_history_summary: Born in Jiangsu, China; emigrated to Vancouver at age 12 after Tiananmen-related family exile of his teacher father. Worked McDonald's and gas-station jobs while studying computer science at McGill, then built trading software for Tokyo Stock Exchange subcontractors and Bloomberg before starting Fusion Systems in Shanghai.
family_context_summary: Parents were schoolteachers in China; father was branded a pro-bourgeois intellectual and exiled to rural areas; family emigrated to Canada when Zhao was 12 and lived modestly in Vancouver.
parent_family_domain_summary: Teaching parents; no documented finance/tech domain transfer.
evidence_summary: Zhao's defining achievement is founding Binance in 2017 (age ~40) and rapidly becoming the largest crypto exchange by volume. No material independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found; Fusion Systems and Bloomberg work came at/after late twenties.

name: Kevin Rose
category: Social news founder (Digg); tech media personality
milestone_by_age_26: No material age-26 milestone found. Digg launched December 5, 2004 when Rose was 27; he became a regular co-host of The Screen Savers in March 2004 (age 27). Earlier TechTV production-assistant/segment work and thebroken podcast (July 2003, age 26) do not rise to an independently material breakout under a conservative bar.
early_history_summary: Born in Shasta County, California; raised largely in Las Vegas; Eagle Scout; dropped out of UNLV computer science in 1998. Moved to San Francisco around 2000 for dot-com work, then joined TechTV's The Screen Savers as a production assistant and on-air tip segment host before co-founding Digg and Revision3.
family_context_summary: Not richly documented in reviewed sources beyond California/Nevada upbringing.
evidence_summary: Rose's defining milestone Digg came at age 27. TechTV work before 26 was supporting/segment-level media exposure without a dated product or company breakout meeting the material bar.

name: Justin Kan
category: Live video / gaming platform co-founder (Justin.tv, Twitch)
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Justin.tv in 2007 at age 23 with Emmett Shear, Michael Seibel, and Kyle Vogt, launching a 24/7 lifecasting experiment that became a major live-video platform and later spun out Twitch.
early_history_summary: Born in Seattle to an ethnically Chinese father (finance director at University of Washington; grew up poor) and a Malaysian-Chinese immigrant mother (former programmer, later real estate). Graduated Yale in 2005 (physics and philosophy), entered Y Combinator's first batch that summer with calendar startup Kiko alongside Emmett Shear, then founded Justin.tv in 2007.
family_context_summary: Upper-middle-class Seattle Chinese-American household by adulthood: father UW finance director, mother former CS programmer turned real estate agent; both parents had poorer origins (father poor Seattle childhood; mother from large Malaysian peasant family).
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother studied computer science and worked as a programmer; father worked in university finance administration—some technical/professional orientation but not a consumer-internet founding network.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Yale, YC first batch, Emmett Shear/Michael Seibel/Kyle Vogt team, San Francisco live-video wave
evidence_summary: Kan combined Yale education, Y Combinator's inaugural batch (Kiko, 2005), and a durable cofounder set to launch Justin.tv at 23—a nationally covered lifecasting product that scaled into the live-video platform later spun into Twitch. Family offered upper-middle-class stability and a mother with CS background; Paul Graham/YC mentorship and SF ecosystem proximity amplified execution. Brother Daniel later co-founded Exec with him, extending the high-trust peer pattern.
starting_point: Born in Seattle to an ethnically Chinese father who grew up poor and became a University of Washington finance director, and a Malaysian-Chinese immigrant mother who worked as a programmer then real estate agent.
current_position: Serial founder and investor; co-runs Goat Capital; previously YC partner; founded Atrium (shut 2020) and NFT/gaming ventures Fractal/Stash; lives as a public tech entrepreneur and YouTuber.

trajectory.event: Entered Y Combinator's first batch with Emmett Shear and calendar startup Kiko; later sold Kiko via eBay auction for roughly $250k+.
Co-founded Justin.tv, broadcasting his life 24/7 via a head-mounted camera and drawing major media attention.
Spun out gaming live streams as TwitchTV public beta; also launched Socialcam mobile video app.
Sold Socialcam to Autodesk for about $60 million.
Amazon acquired Twitch for about $970 million; Kan became a Y Combinator partner.
Launched legal-tech firm Atrium and left YC; Atrium later raised large VC rounds before shutting in 2020.
Launched Solana NFT marketplace Fractal (later Stash).

name: Gabe Newell
milestone_by_age_26: After dropping out of Harvard to join Microsoft (~1983), served as producer/program manager on the first two releases of Microsoft Windows (Windows 1.0 in 1985 at age 23; Windows 2.0 in 1987 at age 24–25), a foundational role on the defining PC operating system of the era.
early_history_summary: Born in Aspen, Colorado, and raised in Davis, California; programmed in high school and entered Harvard around 1980 intending possibly medicine. After visiting his brother at Microsoft, Steve Ballmer urged him to work there; he dropped out and spent 13 years as a programmer and technical executive, including program management on early Windows and later the Doom Windows 95 port.
family_context_summary: Son of Donald Newell; born in Aspen and raised in Davis, California. Detailed class/family financial background not richly documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as a tech-domain transfer; brother worked at Microsoft and introduced him to the company.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Harvard dropout to early Microsoft, Windows program management, Ballmer hire path, Mike Harrington cofounder later
evidence_summary: Newell's age-26 milestone is leadership production/program management on the first Windows releases at early Microsoft—an elite institutional pipeline into the PC software frontier. Brother's Microsoft connection and Ballmer's recruitment catalyzed the path; later Mike Harrington partnership and Microsoft wealth funded Valve. Defining public fame still centers on Valve/Half-Life/Steam after age 26, but the Windows PM role is a dated, material technical leadership milestone within the cutoff.
starting_point: Born in Aspen, Colorado, raised in Davis, California; son of Donald Newell; entered Harvard in the early 1980s before dropping out for Microsoft.
current_position: Co-founder and president of Valve; majority owner of Steam ecosystem; estimated net worth around $11 billion (Forbes 2025); also owns marine research org Inkfish, Starfish Neuroscience, and yacht maker Oceanco.

trajectory.event: Dropped out of Harvard and joined Microsoft after Steve Ballmer encouraged him to work there.
Served as producer/program manager on Microsoft Windows 1.0, the first Windows release.
Continued Windows program management through Windows 2.0 era as an early Microsoft technical executive.
Left Microsoft with Mike Harrington to co-found Valve and fund Half-Life.
Released Half-Life, a critical and commercial breakthrough FPS.
Launched Steam digital distribution, which later dominated PC game downloads.
Received BAFTA Fellowship and AIAS Hall of Fame recognition for industry contributions.

name: Markus Persson
milestone_by_age_26: No material age-26 milestone found. Minecraft first public release was 17 May 2009 at age 29; Wurm Online (with Rolf Jansson) around 2006 was at age ~27, and pre-2005 work was employment as a web designer and Midasplayer/King Flash programmer without an independently notable breakout by 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Stockholm to a Finnish mother (nurse) and Swedish father (railroad worker with mental-health and alcoholism struggles); parents divorced when he was about seven amid food insecurity. Programmed on a Commodore 128 from age seven, made a text adventure at eight, left high school unfinished, and worked web design and game programming jobs through the mid-2000s.
family_context_summary: Working-class Swedish household with parental divorce, paternal alcoholism/bipolar illness, sister's drug issues, and intermittent food insecurity.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a 'nerd' who built a modem and taught him Commodore 128 use—meaningful early computer exposure without professional game-industry status.
evidence_summary: Persson's defining achievement Minecraft arrived at age 29. By age 26 he was a working programmer with long personal practice but without a dated, material public product milestone meeting the eligibility bar.

name: Phil Spencer
milestone_by_age_26: No material age-26 milestone found. Joined Microsoft as an intern in 1988 (age 20) and worked on early CD-ROM titles and consumer productivity products; public leadership of Xbox/Microsoft Gaming came decades later (notably 2014+ Xbox lead; 2022 CEO of Microsoft Gaming).
early_history_summary: Born in Ridgefield, Washington; attended Ridgefield High School and earned a bachelor's in technical and scientific communication from the University of Washington. Interned at Microsoft in 1988 and spent his career there across CD-ROM titles (Encarta), Microsoft Money, Works, Picture It!, and later Xbox studio leadership.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond Washington State origin.
evidence_summary: Spencer's career is a long Microsoft internal climb; defining Xbox leadership and CEO of Microsoft Gaming roles arrived far after age 26. Early intern/CD-ROM work is employment without a material personal public milestone by the cutoff.
